answer: In a design market, a buyer commissions a lagoon poster with a raven silhouette and a specified pigment palette. Artists commit their files before review; a perceptual hash groups near-identical designs, and randomly assigned reviewers assess each group. Only one payment can be claimed per group, so ten aliases using the same artwork earn once. To multiply payouts, an attacker needs ten distinct, acceptable designs and must pay review fees. Similarity checks can merge honest work, and colluding reviewers may favor copies; publish appeals and rotate reviewers.
